Good things take a little time.
When enabled, YouTube Focus uses Android’s AccessibilityService API to read visible text and controls in the YouTube app.
Data accessed: names, including channel or account display names; personal identifiers such as YouTube @handles; and other content visible on screen, such as video titles, descriptions, and comments.

Why: SAFAR uses channel names, handles, player controls, and screen text to identify channels, detect videos and Shorts, apply your blocking choices, and measure viewing time. It does not use comments or unrelated account text to identify channels.
To apply your choices, SAFAR may pause playback, leave blocked content, and show blocking controls over YouTube.

What is saved: channel names or @handles in your productive list stay on this device. Daily viewing totals sync to SAFAR for analytics. Raw screen text, video titles, descriptions, and comments are not uploaded by this feature.
This access is optional. You can switch it off anytime in Android Settings → Accessibility → SAFAR YouTube Focus.
